title: Cross-Tumor Transportability of the Hemo-Eosinophil Inflammation Index Reveals a Glioblastoma-Specific Inflammatory Phenotype
content: Background: To evaluate whether the original Hemo-Eosinophil Inflammation (HEI) Index is prognostically transportable to IDH-wildtype glioblastoma (GBM) and whether component decomposition identifies a disease-specific inflammatory phenotype. Methods: We retrospectively analyzed 127 patients with IDH-wildtype GBM treated with radiotherapy and concurrent temozolomide. Original HEI assigns one adverse point for hemoglobin < 12 g/dL, systemic immune-inflammation index (SII) >560, and eosinophils >=100 cells/µL. Cox regression, restricted cubic splines, 2,000 bootstrap resamples, and Harrell C-index were used. Exploratory score development followed component analysis and cut-point stability assessment. Results: Original HEI was evaluable in 124 patients and was not associated with OS after adjustment (HR 1.50, 95% CI 0.95-2.37; p=0.082), with non-proportional hazards. SII was adverse (HR 1.24 per doubling; p=0.027), hemoglobin neutral, and higher eosinophils favorable (HR 0.62 per +100 cells/µL; p=0.030). An exploratory score assigning one point for SII >800 and eosinophils < =10 cells/µL identified 34, 44, and 44 patients with scores 0, 1, and 2; median OS was 20.9, 13.7, and 8.67 months. Adjusted HR was 1.38 per point (95% CI 1.04-1.83; p=0.027). Clinical-model C-index increased from 0.691 to 0.714; optimism-corrected values were 0.675 and 0.695. Conclusions: The original HEI was not directly transportable to GBM. Its failure reflected divergent component biology rather than absence of systemic prognostic information. A high-SII/eosinopenia phenotype showed exploratory prognostic value and requires external validation.
